title: Digital Eye Strain: Causes, Symptoms, and the 20-20-20 Rule
content:
Digital eye strain (also known as Computer Vision Syndrome) is a cluster of ocular and vision-related discomforts resulting from prolonged uninterrupted viewing of digital monitors, laptops, tablets, and mobile screens.

Common Signs and Symptoms:
- Eye fatigue, heaviness, or tired eyes.
- Burning, stinging, or gritty sensation (dry eyes due to reduced blinking rate; people blink about 66% less frequently when looking at digital screens).
- Intermittent blurred vision or difficulty refocusing between distant and near objects.
- Mild headache behind or around the eyes.
- Neck, shoulder, and upper back tightness caused by awkward posture.

Key Relief Strategies and the 20-20-20 Rule:
1. The 20-20-20 Rule: Every 20 minutes spent viewing a screen, pause and shift your visual focus to an object located at least 20 feet away for a full 20 seconds. This allows the ciliary accommodation muscles inside your eyes to relax completely.
2. Optimize Screen Ergonomics: Position your display screen roughly an arm's length away (20 to 28 inches) and slightly below eye level (the center of the screen 4 to 5 inches below horizontal eye gaze).
3. Control Glare and Lighting: Adjust room lighting so it is roughly equal in intensity to the monitor display. Use anti-glare screen filters or reposition monitors away from unshaded windows.
4. Conscious Blinking & Lubricating Drops: Make a conscious effort to complete full blinks frequently, or use preservative-free artificial tear eye drops to refresh ocular moisture.

Seek an in-person examination by an optometrist or ophthalmologist if eye pain is severe, if you see flashes of light or floating spots, or if vision becomes persistently double or impaired.
source_name: American Optometric Association (AOA) & American Academy of Ophthalmology
